names = ["Peter", "Eric", "Alice", "Arnold"]
smoothies = ["watermelon", "desert", "cherry", "dragonfruit"]
colors = ["green", "white", "red", "yellow"]

# Index helpers
idx = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(names)}
sidx = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(smoothies)}
cidx = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(colors)}

# Variables: attribute index for each house (0‑based house numbers)
name_at = [Int(f"name_{i}") for i in range(4)]
smooth_at = [Int(f"smooth_{i}") for i in range(4)]
color_at = [Int(f"color_{i}") for i in range(4)]

s = Solver()

# Domain constraints
for var in name_at + smooth_at + color_at:
    s.add(Or([var == i for i in range(4)]))

# All‑different constraints for each category
s.add(Distinct(name_at))
s.add(Distinct(smooth_at))
s.add(Distinct(color_at))

# 1. Dragonfruit lover is Eric

    s.add(Implies(smooth_at[h] == sidx["dragonfruit"], name_at[h] == idx["Eric"]))
    s.add(Implies(name_at[h] == idx["Eric"], smooth_at[h] == sidx["dragonfruit"]))

# 2. Cherry smoothie is in house 2 (index 1)
s.add(smooth_at[1] == sidx["cherry"])

# 3. Dragonfruit smoothie is in house 4 (index 3)
s.add(smooth_at[3] == sidx["dragonfruit"])

# 4. Arnold is the Watermelon smoothie lover
for h in range(4):
    s.add(Implies(name_at[h] == idx["Arnold"], smooth_at[h] == sidx["watermelon"]))
    s.add(Implies(smooth_at[h] == sidx["watermelon"], name_at[h] == idx["Arnold"]))

# 5. White color is in house 1 (index 0)

# 6. Peter loves white

    s.add(Implies(name_at[h] == idx["Peter"], color_at[h] == cidx["white"]))
    s.add(Implies(color_at[h] == cidx["white"], name_at[h] == idx["Peter"]))

from z3 import *

# Define domains
houses = range(1, 7)

# Attributes
names = ["Carol", "Bob", "Peter", "Eric", "Alice", "Arnold"]
lunches = ["stir fry", "grilled cheese", "soup", "spaghetti", "stew", "pizza"]
styles = ["colonial", "victorian", "craftsman", "mediterranean", "ranch", "modern"]

# Variables: position of each attribute (house number)
name_pos = {n: Int(f"pos_name_{n}") for n in names}
lunch_pos = {l: Int(f"pos_lunch_{l.replace(' ', '_')}") for l in lunches}
style_pos = {s: Int(f"pos_style_{s}") for s in styles}

s = Solver()

# Domain constraints
for v in list(name_pos.values()) + list(lunch_pos.values()) + list(style_pos.values()):
    s.add(v >= 1, v <= 6)

# All-different within each category
s.add(Distinct(*name_pos.values()))
s.add(Distinct(*lunch_pos.values()))
s.add(Distinct(*style_pos.values()))

# Clues
s.add(style_pos["ranch"] == 5)                                 # 1
s.add(style_pos["modern"] != 1)                                # 2
s.add(lunch_pos["stir fry"] == name_pos["Peter"] - 1)          # 3
s.add(Abs(style_pos["craftsman"] - name_pos["Arnold"]) == 2)   # 4
s.add(lunch_pos["grilled cheese"] == style_pos["victorian"])  # 5
s.add(lunch_pos["stew"] == style_pos["colonial"])              # 6
s.add(lunch_pos["soup"] == lunch_pos["pizza"] - 1)             # 7
s.add(name_pos["Alice"] == lunch_pos["stew"])                  # 8
s.add(Abs(style_pos["modern"] - name_pos["Arnold"]) == 3)      # 9
s.add(lunch_pos["stew"] != 6)                                  #10
s.add(lunch_pos["spaghetti"] == name_pos["Bob"])              #11
s.add(lunch_pos["grilled cheese"] == 2)                       #12
s.add(name_pos["Carol"] != 4)                                 #13

# Solve
if s.check() == sat:
    m = s.model()
    # Build inverse maps for printing
    house_to_name = {}
    house_to_lunch = {}
    house_to_style = {}
    for n in names:
        house_to_name[m[name_pos[n]].as_long()] = n
    for l in lunches:
        house_to_lunch[m[lunch_pos[l]].as_long()] = l
    for st in styles:
        house_to_style[m[style_pos[st]].as_long()] = st

    for i in range(1, 7):
        print(f"House {i}: {house_to_name[i]}, {house_to_lunch[i]}, {house_to_style[i]}")
else:
    print("No solution found.")

pets = ['hamster', 'dog', 'cat', 'rabbit', 'fish', 'bird']

# Create Z3 Int variables: each attribute value maps to a house number

music_var = {m: Int(f"music_{m.replace(' ', '_')}") for m in musics}

phone_var = {p: Int(f"phone_{p.replace(' ', '_')}") for p in phones}

#12. hip hop music lover = Samsung Galaxy S21 user

#13. Carol and Peter are next to each other
s.add(Abs(name_var['Carol'] - name_var['Peter']) == 1)
#14. OnePlus 9 user is Peter

#15. hamster not in first house

#17. two houses between Carol and Alice (distance 3)

#18. dog owner is in house 5
s.add(pet_var['dog'] == 5)
#19. modern house = Eric

#20. Peter lives in colonial house

heights = ["very tall", "tall", "super tall", "average", "very short", "short"]

           "iphone 13", "huawei p50", "xiaomi mi 11"]

# ----- Variables: position of each attribute (1..6) -----
name_pos   = {n: Int(f"pos_name_{n}")   for n in names}
height_pos = {h: Int(f"pos_height_{h}") for h in heights}
phone_pos  = {p: Int(f"pos_phone_{p}")  for p in phones}

s = Solver()

# Domain constraints and all-different within each category
for d in (list(name_pos.values()) + list(height_pos.values()) + list(phone_pos.values())):
    s.add(d >= 1, d <= 6)

s.add(Distinct(*name_pos.values()))
s.add(Distinct(*height_pos.values()))
s.add(Distinct(*phone_pos.values()))

# 2. Peter is somewhere to the left of the person who uses an iPhone 13.

s.add(height_pos["very short"] > phone_pos["google pixel 6"])

# 4. Carol is the person who is very tall.

from z3 import *

# Enumerations
names = ["Eric", "Alice", "Arnold", "Peter"]
colors = ["red", "green", "white", "yellow"]
animals = ["fish", "horse", "cat", "bird"]

# Index helpers
Eric, Alice, Arnold, Peter = range(4)
red, green, white, yellow = range(4)
fish, horse, cat, bird = range(4)

# Variables: house i (0..3) has a name, color, animal (as ints)
name = [Int(f"name_{i}") for i in range(4)]
color = [Int(f"color_{i}") for i in range(4)]
animal = [Int(f"animal_{i}") for i in range(4)]

s = Solver()

# Domains
for i in range(4):
    s.add(And(name[i] >= 0, name[i] <= 3))
    s.add(And(color[i] >= 0, color[i] <= 3))
    s.add(And(animal[i] >= 0, animal[i] <= 3))

# All-different constraints for each category
s.add(Distinct(name))
s.add(Distinct(color))
s.add(Distinct(animal))

# Helper position variables
alice_pos = Int("alice_pos")
peter_pos = Int("peter_pos")
red_pos = Int("red_pos")
cat_pos = Int("cat_pos")
green_pos = Int("green_pos")
white_pos = Int("white_pos")

# Link positions to arrays
for i in range(4):
    s.add(Implies(name[i] == Alice, alice_pos == i))
    s.add(Implies(name[i] == Peter, peter_pos == i))
    s.add(Implies(color[i] == red, red_pos == i))
    s.add(Implies(animal[i] == cat, cat_pos == i))
    s.add(Implies(color[i] == green, green_pos == i))
    s.add(Implies(color[i] == white, white_pos == i))

# Clue 1: Alice and Peter are next to each other
s.add(Abs(alice_pos - peter_pos) == 1)

# Clue 2: red is directly left of cat lover
s.add(cat_pos == red_pos + 1)

# Clue 3: green color person keeps horses
for i in range(4):
    s.add(Implies(color[i] == green, animal[i] == horse))
    s.add(Implies(animal[i] == horse, color[i] == green))

# Clue 4: Arnold loves white
for i in range(4):
    s.add(Implies(name[i] == Arnold, color[i] == white))

# Clue 5: green is directly left of white
s.add(white_pos == green_pos + 1)

# Clue 6: Peter's favorite color is green
for i in range(4):
    s.add(Implies(name[i] == Peter, color[i] == green))

# Clue 7: Eric is the bird keeper
for i in range(4):
    s.add(Implies(name[i] == Eric, animal[i] == bird))

# Solve
if s.check() == sat:
    m = s.model()
    for i in range(4):
        n = names[m[name[i]].as_long()]
        c = colors[m[color[i]].as_long()]
        a = animals[m[animal[i]].as_long()]
        print(f"House {i+1}: {n}, {c}, {a}")
else:
    print("No solution found.")

musics = ['jazz', 'rock', 'classical', 'pop']

music_vars = {m: Int(f"house_{m}") for m in musics}

s = Solver()

# Domain constraints: each variable is between 1 and 4

s.add(Distinct(*music_vars.values()))

from z3 import *

# ----- Data -----
names = ['Eric', 'Peter', 'Alice', 'Bob', 'Arnold']
musics = ['rock', 'pop', 'hip hop', 'jazz', 'classical']

# ----- Variables -----
name_pos = {n: Int(f"pos_{n}") for n in names}
music_pos = {m: Int(f"pos_{m.replace(' ', '_')}") for m in musics}

solver = Solver()

# Domain constraints: positions are 1..5
for v in list(name_pos.values()) + list(music_pos.values()):
    solver.add(v >= 1, v <= 5)

# All names occupy distinct houses; all musics occupy distinct houses
solver.add(Distinct(*name_pos.values()))
solver.add(Distinct(*music_pos.values()))

# ----- Clues -----
# 1. Peter is the person who loves hip‑hop music.
solver.add(music_pos['hip hop'] == name_pos['Peter'])

# 2. The person who loves pop music is in the first house.
solver.add(music_pos['pop'] == 1)

# 3. The person who loves rock music is somewhere to the left of the person who loves classical music.
solver.add(music_pos['rock'] < music_pos['classical'])

# 4. Arnold is not in the fifth house.
solver.add(name_pos['Arnold'] != 5)

# 5. Eric is directly left of Alice.
solver.add(name_pos['Eric'] + 1 == name_pos['Alice'])

# 6. The person who loves rock music is directly left of Alice.
solver.add(music_pos['rock'] + 1 == name_pos['Alice'])

# 7. Alice is the person who loves jazz music.
solver.add(music_pos['jazz'] == name_pos['Alice'])

# 8. The person who loves jazz music is not in the third house.
solver.add(music_pos['jazz'] != 3)

# ----- Solve -----
if solver.check() == sat:
    m = solver.model()
    # Build reverse look‑ups
    house_to_name = {}
    house_to_music = {}
    for n in names:
        house = m[name_pos[n]].as_long()
        house_to_name[house] = n
    for mu in musics:
        house = m[music_pos[mu]].as_long()
        house_to_music[house] = mu
    # Print solution
    for house in range(1, 6):
        print(f"House {house}: {house_to_name[house]}, {house_to_music[house]}")
else:
    print("No solution found.")

s.add(Distinct(Music))
s.add(Distinct(Month))
s.add(Distinct(Smoothie))

              "science fiction", "biography"]
smoothies_list = ["cherry", "desert", "lime", "watermelon",
                  "blueberry", "dragonfruit"]
animals_list = ["fish", "rabbit", "bird", "cat", "horse", "dog"]
music_list = ["classical", "hip hop", "country", "jazz", "rock", "pop"]
cigars_list = ["prince", "dunhill", "blends", "pall mall",
               "blue master", "yellow monster"]

# ---------- Create Z3 variables (position 0‑5) ----------
def mk_vars(items):
    return {itm: Int(itm.replace(" ", "_")) for itm in items}

names   = mk_vars(names_list)
books   = mk_vars(books_list)
smooth  = mk_vars(smoothies_list)
animals = mk_vars(animals_list)
music   = mk_vars(music_list)
cigars  = mk_vars(cigars_list)

solver = Solver()

# ---------- Domain and all‑different constraints ----------
all_groups = [names, books, smooth, animals, music, cigars]
for group in all_groups:
    for v in group.values():
        solver.add(v >= 0, v < 6)
    solver.add(Distinct(list(group.values())))

# ---------- Encode clues ----------
# 1. blends == fantasy
solver.add(cigars["blends"] == books["fantasy"])

# 2. biography == desert
solver.add(books["biography"] == smooth["desert"])

# 3. two houses between pop and country → distance 3
solver.add(Abs(music["pop"] - music["country"]) == 3)

# 4. rabbit in third house (index 2)
solver.add(animals["rabbit"] == 2)

# 5. Arnold is the bird keeper
solver.add(names["Arnold"] == animals["bird"])

# 6. country music in fifth house (index 4)
solver.add(music["country"] == 4)

# 7. mystery not in first house
solver.add(books["mystery"] != 0)

# 8. lime not in third house
solver.add(smooth["lime"] != 2)

# 9. fish right of rock
solver.add(animals["fish"] > music["rock"])

#10. prince left of cherry
solver.add(cigars["prince"] < smooth["cherry"])

#11. Bob is the cat lover
solver.add(names["Bob"] == animals["cat"])

#12. Eric likes cherry smoothies
solver.add(names["Eric"] == smooth["cherry"])

#13. Yellow Monster in sixth house (index 5)
solver.add(cigars["yellow monster"] == 5)

#14. prince == dragonfruit
solver.add(cigars["prince"] == smooth["dragonfruit"])

#15. Carol directly left of Arnold
solver.add(names["Carol"] + 1 == names["Arnold"])

#16. blue master directly left of classical
solver.add(cigars["blue master"] + 1 == music["classical"])

#17. classical == historical fiction
solver.add(music["classical"] == books["historical fiction"])

#18. dunhill next to science fiction
solver.add(Abs(cigars["dunhill"] - books["science fiction"]) == 1)

#19. horse directly left of Peter
solver.add(animals["horse"] + 1 == names["Peter"])

#20. watermelon == cat
solver.add(smooth["watermelon"] == animals["cat"])

#21. blends directly left of jazz
solver.add(cigars["blends"] + 1 == music["jazz"])

#22. cat in first house (index 0)
solver.add(animals["cat"] == 0)

#23. desert == jazz
solver.add(smooth["desert"] == music["jazz"])

#24. lime directly left of fish
solver.add(smooth["lime"] + 1 == animals["fish"])

#25. blue master not in fifth house (index 4)
solver.add(cigars["blue master"] != 4)

# ---------- Solve ----------
if solver.check() == sat:
    m = solver.model()
    # Build inverse maps: position -> attribute
    inv = {}
    for cat_name, group in zip(
        ["Name", "Book", "Smoothie", "Animal", "Music", "Cigar"],
        [names, books, smooth, animals, music, cigars]
    ):
        inv[cat_name] = {m[v].as_long(): k for k, v in group.items()}

phone = [Int(f"phone_{i}") for i in range(3)]
occ = [Int(f"occ_{i}") for i in range(3)]
hobby = [Int(f"hobby_{i}") for i in range(3)]
animal = [Int(f"animal_{i}") for i in range(3)]

s = Solver()

# domain constraints
for var in name + phone + occ + hobby + animal:
    s.add(var >= 0, var <= 2)

s.add(Distinct(phone))
s.add(Distinct(occ))
s.add(Distinct(hobby))
s.add(Distinct(animal))

))

from z3 import *

# Houses are numbered 1..6
houses = range(1, 7)

# Helper to create an integer variable constrained to 1..6
def var(name):
    v = Int(name)
    return v

# ---- Variables for each attribute value ----
# Names
Peter = var('Peter')
Eric  = var('Eric')
Alice = var('Alice')
Carol = var('Carol')
Bob   = var('Bob')
Arnold= var('Arnold')

# Animals
horse = var('horse')
fish  = var('fish')
cat   = var('cat')
bird  = var('bird')
dog   = var('dog')
rabbit= var('rabbit')

# Birthday months
sept = var('sept')
mar  = var('mar')
jan  = var('jan')
feb  = var('feb')
april= var('april')
may  = var('may')

# Mothers
Holly   = var('Holly')
Sarah   = var('Sarah')
Penny   = var('Penny')
Kailyn  = var('Kailyn')
Aniya   = var('Aniya')
Janelle = var('Janelle')

# Vacations
beach    = var('beach')
cruise   = var('cruise')
cultural = var('cultural')
camping  = var('camping')
city     = var('city')
mountain = var('mountain')

s = Solver()

# ---- Domain constraints (1..6) ----
all_vars = [Peter, Eric, Alice, Carol, Bob, Arnold,
            horse, fish, cat, bird, dog, rabbit,
            sept, mar, jan, feb, april, may,
            Holly, Sarah, Penny, Kailyn, Aniya, Janelle,
            beach, cruise, cultural, camping, city, mountain]

for v in all_vars:
    s.add(And(v >= 1, v <= 6))

# ---- All-different constraints within each category ----
s.add(Distinct(Peter, Eric, Alice, Carol, Bob, Arnold))
s.add(Distinct(horse, fish, cat, bird, dog, rabbit))
s.add(Distinct(sept, mar, jan, feb, april, may))
s.add(Distinct(Holly, Sarah, Penny, Kailyn, Aniya, Janelle))
s.add(Distinct(beach, cruise, cultural, camping, city, mountain))

# ---- Clues ----
# 1. February == fish
s.add(feb == fish)

# 2. May is to the right of Penny
s.add(may > Penny)

# 3. beach == Peter
s.add(beach == Peter)

# 4. Janelle == Carol
s.add(Janelle == Carol)

# 5. rabbit == Bob
s.add(rabbit == Bob)

# 6. rabbit == may
s.add(rabbit == may)

# 7. Kailyn is in house 4
s.add(Kailyn == 4)

# 8. camping == cat
s.add(camping == cat)

# 9. cruise == 6
s.add(cruise == 6)

#10. april == dog
s.add(april == dog)

#11. Alice == Aniya
s.add(Alice == Aniya)

#12. May and Sarah are adjacent
s.add(Or(may == Sarah + 1, may == Sarah - 1))

#13. Holly == cat
s.add(Holly == cat)

#14. Two houses between March and rabbit -> distance 3
s.add(Or(mar == rabbit + 3, mar == rabbit - 3))

#15. dog is directly left of horse
s.add(dog + 1 == horse)

#16. February is in house 2
s.add(feb == 2)

#17. rabbit is to the right of cultural
s.add(rabbit > cultural)

#18. Carol is in house 2
s.add(Carol == 2)

#19. sept == city
s.add(sept == city)

#20. Eric != 1
s.add(Eric != 1)

# ---- Solve ----
if s.check() == sat:
    m = s.model()
    # Build reverse look‑ups: house -> attribute string
    house_info = {i: {} for i in houses}

    # Helper to fill a category
    def fill(category_vars, attr_name):
        for attr, var_obj in category_vars.items():
            house = m[var_obj].as_long()
            house_info[house][attr_name] = attr

    fill({'Peter':Peter, 'Eric':Eric, 'Alice':Alice,
          'Carol':Carol, 'Bob':Bob, 'Arnold':Arnold},
         'Name')
    fill({'horse':horse, 'fish':fish, 'cat':cat, 'bird':bird,
          'dog':dog, 'rabbit':rabbit},
         'Animal')
    fill({'sept':sept, 'mar':mar, 'jan':jan, 'feb':feb,
          'april':april, 'may':may},
         'Month')
    fill({'Holly':Holly, 'Sarah':Sarah, 'Penny':Penny,
          'Kailyn':Kailyn, 'Aniya':Aniya, 'Janelle':Janelle},
         'Mother')
    fill({'beach':beach, 'cruise':cruise, 'cultural':cultural,
          'camping':camping, 'city':city, 'mountain':mountain},
         'Vacation')

    # Print houses in order
    for i in houses:
        info = house_info[i]
        print(f"House {i}: {info['Name']}, {info['Animal']}, {info['Month']}, {info['Mother']}, {info['Vacation']}")
else:
    print("No solution found")
